author: fruffy
body:
Consolidate several packet sizing options into one. Packet sizes are now defined as range (`[min]:[max]`). The maximum packet size is now jumbo frame size (9000 byte). Extensions which do not support this size will have to override or implement their own checks (see the eBPF back end). 

Fixes #3559.

author: myxmxm
body:
What does this PR do:
Make the news list on the home screen clickable.
After clicking news from the news list on the home screen, the user will be navigated to a detailed view of that news.
From there, users are able to see all comments posted to that news, users are able to post their own comment, and add or remove that news to their favorite list.

      • Early exit on broken .next in missed cases of { Iterator, AsyncIterator }.from, proposal-iterator-helpers/232
    • Added self polyfill as a part of The Minimum Common Web Platform API, specification, #1118
    • Added inverse option to core-js-compat, #1119
    • Added format option to core-js-builder, #1120
    • Added NodeJS 19.0 compat data
    • Added Deno 1.26 and 1.27 compat data
    • Added Opera Android 72 compat data mapping
    • Updated Electron 22 compat data mapping
  • 3.25.5 - 2022-10-03
    • Fixed regression with an error on reuse of some built-in methods from another realm, #1133
  • 3.25.4 - 2022-10-02
    • Added a workaround of a Nashorn bug with Function.prototype.{ call, apply, bind } on string methods, #1128
    • Updated lists of [Serializable] and [Transferable] objects in the structuredClone polyfill. Mainly, for better error messages if polyfilling of cloning such types is impossible
    • Array.prototype.{ group, groupToMap } marked as supported from V8 ~ Chromium 108
    • Added Electron 22 compat data mapping
  • 3.25.3 - 2022-09-25
    • Forced polyfilling of Array.prototype.groupToMap in the pure version for returning wrapped Map instances
    • Fixed existence of Array.prototype.{ findLast, findLastIndex } in /stage/4 entry
    • Added Opera Android 71 compat data mapping
    • Some stylistic changes
  • 3.25.2 - 2022-09-18
    • Considering document.all as a callable in some missed cases
    • Added Safari 16.0 compat data
    • Added iOS Safari 16.0 compat data mapping
    • Fixed some ancient iOS Safari versions compat data mapping
  • 3.25.1 - 2022-09-07
    • Added some fixes and workarounds of FF30- typed arrays bug that does not properly convert objects to numbers
    • Added sideEffects field to core-js-pure package.json for better tree shaking, #1117
    • Dropped semver dependency from core-js-compat
      • semver package (ironically) added a breaking change and dropped NodeJS 8 support in the minor 7.1 version, after that semver in core-js-compat was pinned to 7.0 since for avoiding breaking changes it should support NodeJS 8. However, since core-js-compat is usually used with other packages that use semver dependency, it causes multiple duplications of semver in dependencies. So I decided to remove semver dependency and replace it with a couple of simple helpers.
    • Added Bun 0.1.6-0.1.11 compat data
    • Added Deno 1.25 compat data mapping

Resolves #19.

Introduces the following:
- Added `fetch_content` method to retrieve file contents via the [Repository contents API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/contents).
- Added `build_sponsor_json` method to construct the sponsor section in the [cores.yml](https://github.com/joshcampbell191/openfpga-cores-inventory/blob/master/_data/cores.yml) based on the [`FUNDING.yml`](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/displaying-a-sponsor-button-in-your-repository#about-funding-files) while using [community health files](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/setting-up-your-project-for-healthy-contributions/creating-a-default-community-health-file) as a backup.
- Added logic to update the `sponsor` section when adding / updating a core.
  - It should also update the `sponsor` section if the core hasn't changed (since the `FUNDING.yml` file is controlled outside of the core releases)

Overall, I'm pretty happy with how the code turned out. Feel free to correct anything I might've missed as I'm fairly new to Ruby.

author: kvinwang
body:
This PR implements `weighted local cache` for fat contracts.

We allocate about 20MiB amount of memory for a single pRuntime instance. And each contract can share part of the memory by the ratio of its weight(the same weight used by the query scheduler, which was set by the tokenomic driver).

The local cache implementation is moved into `pink-extension-runtime` so that we can use it in pink unit tests.

body:
Now you can ctrl-click on `Quot` in `#check Quot` and it will jump to the `add_decl_doc Quot` line as though it were the actual definition. (We could jump to the `init_quot` line but that line has to define a bunch of things at once and the documentation isn't as good.)

You can also use `add_decl_doc` for other definitions that lack definition links, although these should not occur unless you are using something like the `kdef` command from #1781.

author: axw
body:
## Motivation/summary

Allow a null `config` attribute in `agent_config` entries, treating it the same as an empty config map.

When no attributes are specified in an APM Agent central config entry, it will be added by APM UI to the APM integration policies as `{}`. Somewhere along the way to APM Server this is translated to `null`.

## Checklist

- [x] Update [CHANGELOG.asciidoc](https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.asciidoc)
~- [ ] Update [package changelog.yml](https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/blob/main/apmpackage/apm/changelog.yml) (only if changes to `apmpackage` have been made)~
~- [ ] Documentation has been updated~

## How to test these changes

See https://github.com/elastic/apm-server/issues/9545

## Related issues

-->

Resolves: #GITHUB_ISSUE_ID or https://link_to_the_issue_on_discuss.bitrise.io.
-->

We discussed that using `zip` for build artifacts and `tar` for pipeline intermediates is not ideal moving forward due to having to maintain both tools across stacks, so this PR adds support for extracting `zip` archives.

For compatibility with the deploy-to-bitrise-io step version 2.1.3, support for `tar` archives is kept.

### Changes

<!--

The plan moving forward is to consolidate and use `zip` across the board instead of making additional changes to accommodate `tar` in order to avoid having to maintain both tools across stacks. `zip` also gives the benefit of compressing the archive by default.

  compatible with codespaces.

author: thatplguy
body:
Call a new backend API to report initial client telemetry, and include the following additional metadata:
* CLI version
* CLI target architecture
* Whether the CLI was running in a Docker container distributed by Akita
* Whether the CLI was running in a Docker container running on Docker Desktop

The main goal is to detect when customers are running the Akita CLI in Docker Desktop with their service running on the host.  Because Docker Desktop (e.g. on macOS) doesn't support `--network host`, users in this case won't capture any service traffic.  Collecting this metadata lets us display a nicer error in the Akita app.

Depends on https://github.com/akitasoftware/akita-libs/pull/175.

author: michael0x2a
body:
Fixes #11860 (?)

Typeshed is currently unable to import Sequence, MutableSequence, or ByteString from collections.abc within builtins.pyi. It seems this is because:

1. In order to analyze `collections.abc`, we first need to analyze `collections`.

2. Since `collections` is a package containing an `__init__.pyi` file, the `add_implicit_module_attrs` function will try adding the `__path__` variable to the symboltable.

3. The `__path__` variable has type `builtins.str`. But str is a subclass of Sequence, which we have not analyzed yet since we're still in the middle of analyzing `collections` and `collections.abc`.

This diff tries repairing this by:

1. Adding `_collections_abc` and `collections.abc` to the set of special-cased core modules we deliberately process early.

2. Modifying `add_implicit_module_attrs` so it does the same trick we do for the `__doc__` symbol and fall back to using an UnboundType if `builtins.str` is not defined yet.

To be 100% honest, I'm not really sold on this PR for a few reasons:

- I was able to test these changes manually, but wasn't sure how to write tests for them.
- We have 3-4 subtly different lists of "core modules" scattered throughout mypy. For example, see `CORE_BUILTIN_MODULES` in mypy/build.py or try grepping for the string `"typing"` in the mypy dir. Arguably, we should defer landing this PR until we've had a chance to consolidate these lists and confirm there are no additional places where we need to special-case `_collections_abc`, `collections`, and `collections.abc`.
- PEP 585 attempted to declare that we should one day remove entries like Sequence from `typing` module, but this realistically doesn't seem ever achievable given that (a) it would break backwards compat and (b) there doesn't seem to be any incentives for users to proactively switch. In that case, is there any pressing reason to change typeshed?

Regardless, this is a crash and my goal atm is to de-crash mypy, so I'm throwing this over the wall.

### Motivation

Currently, the AoP can't leverage the multi bundles feature, exchanges and queues belonging to one AMQP virtual host are owned by one namespace bundle, they must work on one broker. So the broker can't scale up simply to support increasing exchanges and queues, if users want to use all brokers of a cluster, they need to use different virtual hosts for different exchanges and queues, it's very hard to adjust existing applications and it's not friendly to use.

### Modifications

- support exchange declare
- support queue declare
- support queue bind
- support queue unbind
- support basic publish
- support basic consume

For sql `select * from t1 join t3 on t1.id = t3.id join t2 on t3.id = t2.id`,   wheter colocate join is available need consider column equivalent conduction `t3.id = t1.id = t2.id`.

What's more, for sql `select * from t1 join t3 on t1.id = t3.age and t1.id = t3.id join t2 on t2.id = t3.age and t2.age = t3.age` the order of equivalence predicates(shuffle columns are derived from them) is meaningless, hence it is correct to use a set to save these shuffle pairs. According to the distribution column information of the left and right children, we can build distribution pairs. We can use colocate join is judged by whether all the distribution pairs are exist in the equivalent predicates set.

author: chacha912
body: #### What this PR does / why we need it? - Add `rehypeImageMeta.ts` Next.js's component requires image's width and height properties to [prevent layout shift](https://web.dev/optimize-cls/#images-without-dimensions). [The `rehypeImageMeta` plugin](https://kylepfromer.com/blog/nextjs-image-component-blog/) attaches the image's height and width to its properties. > This only works with the markdown image form, ie: `![image](/path/to/image)` and does not work with JSX components. If you use a JSX image component you will need to figure out the height and width manually. - Add `Next-Image-Export-Optimizer` The [next export with Image API](https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/export-image-api) error occurs when I run `next export` to deploy. So I add [next-image-export-optimizer](https://github.com/Niels-IO/next-image-export-optimizer) to use the Next.js component with optimized images while using the static export functionality. *Alternatively, we can use [another custom loader](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/19065) to use next/image (for maintaining aspect ratio, etc) with no image optimization.* > The library wraps the component of Next.js and automatically creates optimized images using sharp.js at export time. > It uses a custom loader to create a srcset for the that the component of Next.js creates. Then at build/export time, the images inside the public/images folder (as an example) are optimized with sharp.js and copied into the build folder. https://stackoverflow.com/a/71535020 - Add `postcss-path-replace` I used the `post-css-path-replace` plugin to add the base path to the resource's url in CSS. *When defining a [custom PostCSS configuration file](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/customizing-postcss-config#customizing-plugins), Next.js completely disables the [default behavior](https://nextjs.org/docs/advanced-features/customizing-postcss-config#default-behavior). So if we need, we configure all the features manually, including `Autoprefixer`.*

author: jenswikl
body:
This is https://github.com/OP-TEE/optee_os/pull/5247 rebased and updated.

The use case is to make `buf_ta_open()` more resilient to fault injection attacks on the hardware, more specifically glitching attacks. The basic assumption is that glitch can cause one or more instructions in sequence to act as nops when executed. Anything can happen of course but I'm using this approximation to have something more concrete to work with.

The fault mitigations are supposed to add zero overhead unless enabled and if enabled have a  modest overhead.

In this PR I've made fault mitigations enabled by default with `CFG_CORE_FAULT_MITIGATION?=y` in `mk/config.mk`. Should it be disabled by default instead?

author: sjapaget
body:
**Problem**
Previously the logo image in the navbar was not loading correctly in production - the src path was not leading to the image file once the build had been run by vite. 

**Solution**
This was fixed by removing the path which had been hard-coded for the src attribute and replacing it with an import statement that assigns the path to a variable. This variable is then used in the jsx of the navbar to assign the src attribute. 

This way when we run the build process with vite the correct asset paths are assigned and the image is properly loaded.

This PR make sure that an action is executed only on minions having a pending entry in the `ServerAction` table. body:
#### What is the purpose of this change?

Currently the Azure Blob backend has no support for custom headers. This PR allows one to specify the following headers using the `--header-upload` flag:

- Cache-Control
- Content-Disposition
- Content-Encoding
- Content-Language
- Content-Type

These headers are supported by Azure and become properties of the given Azure blob. This also allows one to overwrite the content-type, since that is currently derived from the local file.

No

author: jasperzhong
body:
## Changes 

1. significantly speed up insert_edges by reducing the number of launching cuda kernels
2. implement adaptive block size method
3. add some functions for metrics (i.e., average linked list length, graph edge data memory, and graph metadata graph) 
4. change the default minimal block size to round(|E|/|V|) for each dataset. 
5. reduce graph metadata memory usage. The DoublyLinkedList data structure (on device) only keeps a pointer to the tail block now. 

The **adaptive block size** method is based on the average edges per insertion for each vertex, denoted as $\tilde{m_i}$. The method will allocate a block with a block size of $\text{NextPowOf2}(\tilde{m_i})$. The method is **used by default now** but can be optionally disabled (see benchmark_build_graph.py). 

## Evaluation on adaptive block size method

g4dn.metal. benchmark on GDELT. ingestion_batch_size = 1M. 

| | build time | average linked list length | graph edge data memory (MB)  |  graph metadata (on GPU) memory (MB) | 
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 
| w/o |252.58s |  22.74  | 7322.65MB | 22.28MB |
| w/ adaptive block size | 254.05s | 17.71 | 7346.96MB | 18.16MB |

As the table shows, the adaptive block size method significantly reduces the average linked list length with almost the same graph edge data memory and less graph metadata memory usage.

author: rex-9
body:
### Description

The mobile web application where users can manage their budget: users have a list of transactions associated with a category so that the owner can see how much money they spent and on what. 

This Ruby on Rails application allows the user to:
- register and log in, so that the data is private to them.
- introduce new transactions associated with a category.
- see the money spent on each category.

### Project requirements

#### Design
- Followed these [design guidelines](https://www.behance.net/gallery/19759151/Snapscan-iOs-design-and-branding?tracking_source=), including:
  - Colors.
  - Typography: font face, size, and weight.
  - Layout: composition and space between elements.

Original design idea by [Gregoire Vella on Behance](https://www.behance.net/gregoirevella).

The [Creative Commons license of the design](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/) is added to the project and gave appropriate credit to the author in the README file.

#### Interactions
- Splash screen
  - A simple page with the name of the app, and links to the signup and log-in pages.

- Sign up and login pages
  - The user is able to register in the app with full name, email, and password (all mandatory).
  - The user can log into the app using email and password.
  - If the user is not logged in, they can't access pages that require the user to be logged in (all the pages described below).

- Home page (categories page)
  - When the user logs in, they are presented with the categories page.
  - For each category, the user can see their name, icon, and the total amount of all the transactions that belong to that category.
  - When the user clicks (or taps) on a category item, the application navigates to the transactions page for that category.
  - There is a button "add a new category" at the bottom that brings the user to the page to create a new category.

- Transactions page
  - For a given category, the list of transactions is presented, ordered by the most recent.
  - At the top of the page, the user could see the total amount for the category (the sum of all of the amounts of the transactions in that category).
  - There is a button "add a new transaction" at the bottom that brings the user to the page to create a new transaction.
  - When the user clicks on the "Back" button (<), the user navigates to the home page.

- "Add a new category" page
  - The user fills out a form to create a new category, indicating their name and icon (both mandatory).
  - The user clicks (or taps) the "Save" button to create the new category, and is taken to the home page on success.
  - When the user clicks on the "Back" button (<), the user navigates to the home page.

- "Add a new transaction" page
  - The user fills out a form to create a new transaction with:
    - name (mandatory)
    - amount (mandatory)
    - categories (mandatory at least one)
  - The user clicks (or taps) the "Save" button to create the new transaction, and is taken to the transactions page for that category.
  - When the user clicks on the "Back" button (<), the user navigates to the transactions page for that category.

#### Testing requirements
- Created unit and integration tests for all the most important components of the RoR application.

#### Technical requirements

- Used Postgres as your database.
- Used devise for authentication.
- Validated all user input to make sure that anyone with bad intentions cannot compromise your app.
- Used a view template engine of your choice (.erb, .slim, .haml).
- The project is deployed and accessible online.
- The database schema reflects the following structure:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77402992/201668283-fcc9df2b-741a-4cfb-8a2e-a937c955d8ac.png)

### Project documentation

Here is the video presentation of the "Transactions on Rails" project
https://www.loom.com/share/8f05f554375d4621aee04d7c430e3606

It is a video with a **maximum length of 5 minutes**. The content of the video includes:

- a description of the project.
- a demo of the project features.
- highlights of some interesting piece of code or something I built that I am very proud of.

author: thepiachu
body:
<!-- Write **BELOW** The Headers and **ABOVE** The comments else it may not be viewable. -->

## About The Pull Request

I was playing a bit of Research lately and noticed two problems. First, Marines don't retrieve enough xeno corpses because they don't see the benefit of doing so most of the time. Secondly, when Research actually gets xeno corpses they usually take a small sample to analyse for points and dumps the corpses without using up all the blood, which felt like a waste. So I figured I'd try giving Marines a more tangible reason to go fetch xeno corpses - stims and more explosives!

First, background info. Every Xeno has 560 units of blood in them which is usually split between their Acidic Blood and a Plasma (only exception being hugger, chestburster, Spitter and Trapper Boiler with only acidic bloods). When you have a pheromone in a xeno, you usually get 280 units of it. Here is [a spreadsheet covering what you can get from which caste](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1xKf9r0YFWXPomOM69Ka9JqzXOL7FJYfK2UB_BBTm3jE/edit?usp=sharing). Exceptions are Healer Drone, Hivelord, Praetorian and Queen that have more diluted pheromones, with the last one having 112 units of 3 different ones. So our working number is 280u acid blood and one plasma.

IV Drips take 4 units of liquid out per tick, and you can take a bit more out manually with syringes. It will take a few minutes to process each corpse entirely, even with multiple IVs. You are taking out acidic blood and plasma at the same time, so basically acidic blood is a waste product you give to engineering for them to have some fun.

Xeno stims I based off of the SOF stims - they consume 1 unit per 1 minute, and usually come with a dosage of 5, OD of 15, critical of 25. If you take more than one stim you burn through them quicker. My first draft takes 10 units of plasma and combines it with two other chemicals to make 1 unit of stim. So one corpse gives you 28 minutes of a stim, which I'd expect to be almost 6 5 minute doses depending on how Researchers splice them. Of course, the number can be tweaked, but unless we get some faster way of exsanguinating xenos, the amount of stims you get from the blood might be okay. Will need to test to see how it performs, but it should keep a few researchers busy.

Stims are as follows:
- Purple Plasma Stim (from all drone strains) - heals all kinds of damage (on the level of basic med per type), speeds user up a bit, repairs mechanical limbs, creates some blood, stops a bit of pain. Generally, weaker than Unga Juice but still neat.
- Pheromone Plasma Stim (Hivelord, Prae, Healer Drone, Queen) - heals all kinds of damage even better, good painstopper, creates blood, stops bone breaks.
- Chitin Plasma Stim (Defender, Crusher, Prae Oppressor) - mends broken bones, prevents bone breaks, prevents organ damage
- Catecholamine Plasma Stim (Runner, Lurker, Warrior, Prae Dancer, Ravager, Abomination) - increases speed and reflexes
- Egg Plasma Stim (egg, Eggsac Carrier) - heals internal organs and prevents organ damage
- Neurotoxin Plasma Stim (Sentinel, Boiler, Praetorians minus Dancer, Queen) - boosts reflexes, heals brain and eye damage, shields from neurotoxin
- Royal Plasma Stim (Queen, or Prae + Egg via chem reaction) - faster speed, reflexes, no pain, heal broken bones, heal organs, no broken bones, no organ damage

The last one of course comes from the Royal Plasma, which at best you get 112 off per Queen (plus 112 if you have two eggs to convert royal blood into Royal Plasma, or 187 from Praetorian blood and 3 eggs), so the stim is strong, but you get very few uses of it for completing the very strong objective.

As for the acidic blood, I don't have much experience with explosive chemistry. Based the basic acid blood fuel off off UT-Napalm with longer burn time and some oxidizing, guelling, flowing properties, while the Dark Acid Blood (Queen, Prae) is based off of the Napalm EX which sets even the Queen and Ravager on fire and burns them.

I may be wildly out of whack with the various numbers and properties, so some testing, balancing and feedback will be needed.

<!-- Describe The Pull Request. Please be sure every change is documented or this can delay review and even discourage maintainers from merging your PR! -->

## Why It's Good For The Game

It incentivises Marines to fetch more xeno corpses from the battlefield, which has the knockon effect of incentivising more fultons (IOs will be happy!), so Medevacs and all will be more readily available as well and so on. This means Research will get their cool toys to play with for chem points, Command will get Tech Point kickback for the xeno corpses, and Research will have something to do with all that xeno blood in their fun zone that they will get to share with Engineering, encouraging more inter-department play.

Because those stims would be known recipes Researchers won't have to give detailed instructions each time as to how to use them like they have to with custom chems. Hopefully this will also incentivise Marines to try other chems Research will have in store for them.

So hopefully introducing these chems will have a positive knockon effect on the Marine gameplay helping them play into pushing objectives rather than just shooting everything.

<!-- Please add a short description of why you think these changes would benefit the game. If you can't justify it in words, it might not be worth adding, and may discourage maintainers from reviewing or merging your PR. This section is not strictly required for (non-controversial) fix PRs or backend PRs. -->

## Changelog

<!-- You can use multiple of the same prefix (they're only used for the icon ingame) and delete the unneeded ones. Despite some of the tags, changelogs should generally represent how a player might be affected by the changes rather than a summary of the PR's contents. -->

<!-- If your PR modifies aspects of the game that can be concretely observed by players or admins you should add a changelog. If your change does NOT meet this description, remove this section. Be sure to properly mark your PRs to prevent unnecessary GBP loss. Please note that maintainers freely reserve the right to remove and add tags should they deem it appropriate. You can attempt to finagle the system all you want, but it's best to shoot for clear communication right off the bat. -->

:cl:
add: Added a number of xeno-blood-derived stims. You will need to extract xeno corpses, drain them of their blood and combine the individual reagents with other chemicals to make them. Taking more than one at a time diminishes their effectiveness, but they last a while.
add: Added two flammable chemical reagents based on the xeno acidic blood. Engineering will need to work with Research in order to harness them, but they should prove a useful tool against the xenos!
code: Moved stim reagent code in with other reagent codes.
/:cl:

author: schustmi
body:
There are two changes in this PR:

### Default values for all stack component settings can now be configured on the stack component itself
This is solved by making sure the respective `StackComponentConfig` inherits from the settings class specified for the component. For example:
```python
class MLFlowExperimentTrackerSettings(BaseSettings):
    experiment_name: Optional[str] = None
    nested: bool = False
    ...

class MLFlowExperimentTrackerConfig(
    BaseExperimentTrackerConfig, MLFlowExperimentTrackerSettings
):
    tracking_uri: Optional[str] = None
    tracking_username: Optional[str] = SecretField()
    tracking_password: Optional[str] = SecretField()
    ...
```
The config inherits from the settings, which means that users can now for example specify that all runs using this experiment tracker component should be nested by default:
`zenml experiment-tracker register mlflow --flavor=mlflow --nested=True`

This default value can then be overwritten as before by specifying settings on a step/pipeline/run:
```python
@pipeline(
    settings={
        "experiment_tracker.mlflow": MLFlowExperimentTrackerSettings(nested=False)
    }
)
def my_pipeline(...):
    ...
```

### Update to existing stack components

Existing stack component configurations which are "dynamic" and make sense to be configurable on a run-by-run basis were included as settings for that component. Due to technical limitations this right now isn't possible for all options as settings can only be configured when running a pipeline, and not for example when calling `zenml stack up`.

body:
Initial implementation of my suggestion in https://github.com/hapijs/hapi/issues/4388#issuecomment-1312476374.

I have made no changes to the DT typings, which still target v20. I only changed the `@types/hapi__mimos` dependency to `@hapi/mimos`. The version label is copied from the current DT npm release.

While I have imported the DT test suite, I haven't done anything to run it. I have only implemented a very barebones proof-of-concept `test/index.ts` test.

FYI, I haven't tested how this actually works once published, and npm-installed into a project.

Note that I have used the npm *workspaces* feature to improve the ergonomics. This means that the `@hapi/hapi-typings` module lives inside the main hapi repo without any fuss, making it possible to add typings in a single PR along with new hapi features. The main challenge will probably be to remember to actually publish the updated typings with hapi releases, but this should be fixable with a publish script.

author: nberth
body:
I've recently come across some COBOL source files *apparently* targeting MicroFocus, where comments could be seen as lines starting with a `*` after a `$ SET SOURCEFORMAT"FREE"` directive. This appears to be backed up by https://www.microfocus.com/documentation/visual-cobol/vc50pu7/VS2019/HRLHLHINTR01U008.html .
This PR is a suggestion to handle `*`|`/`-starting lines as comments when the `-fmfcomment` is given, even in FREE reference source format.

The space between `$` and `SET` in the directive is neither documented not supported by GnuCOBOL. I'm not sure whether this is actually allowed.

author: leostera
body:
Hello folks 👋🏽 

While working on [warp.build](https://warp.build) I was playing around with the hex.pm API and found out that the file list, while it seems to be present in most packages metadata.config files, isn't part of the release responses.

I recognize that this might be expensive, since some packages may have large lists of files, but it can also be useful for tooling to recognize what package a particular file comes from. Especially in Erlang, it'd be useful to map a module to a file, or to use this list to map header files to packages.

I'll understand if this isn't something we want in the API, but after going back through the history of that file down to ~2006, I couldn't find any rationale for not including it, so I figured I'd open up the PR to have a discussion around it.

wdyt?

author: ivastar
body:
Hi Gabe,

(CC @jdavies-st, @BSGalvan)

This pull requests makes a number of changes that improve the packaging and installation of `grizli`. The changes include:

- Make changes such that `pip` installs all the dependencies together with the package. All dependencies are specified in `setup.cfg`. Optional dependencies (e.g., `test` and `aws`) are only installed when the flag is used. There is no longer a need to create an environment and manage dependencies with conda (environment is still recommended).
- The package is automatically built upon installation using modern PEP517-compliant packaging tools. 
- Remove custom versioning code based on git tag, use the standard `setuptools-scm` instead.  Works the same way, but maintained by the folks who run pypi.org.
- Replace `lacosmicx` with `astroscrappy`: same developer, same code, same API but maintained.
- Update the function that symlinks the templates to symlink the whole directory rather than individual files.
- Add a GitHub actions workflow which builds the wheels and (upon a tagged release) publishes to PyPI. You need to create and save PyPI token in order for this to work. See instructions [here](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/publishing-package-distribution-releases-using-github-actions-ci-cd-workflows/).
- Update the installation docs.
- Fix issues with tests.
- Minor clean-up.
 
One issue we couldn't resolve is the installation of `eazy-py`. Currently (in this PR) `eazy` is being pip-installed (via `setup.cfg`) but also the manual instructions are in the documentation. Seems like `eazy-py` is released to PyPI  but the templates from the original [eazy-photoz](https://github.com/gbrammer/eazy-photoz) repo are not downloaded with that installation. This can be fixed by (for example) adding a function that downloads the templates only (if this is all you need from the `eazy-photoz` repo) rather than making it a subpackage. It doesn't make sense to release `eazy-py` every time you update the templates and filters. Happy to edit this pull request (if you prefer to keep the manual `eazy-py` installation) or make a pull request to `eazy-py` with a proposed solution.

All manual installations (except for `hstcal`) can be removed if `tristars` and `reprocess_wfc3` are also released to PyPI and `pyregion` is replaced with `astropy.regions`. `pyregion` seems to be suffering maintenance issues and while it pip-installs fine on OSX it fails to install in the test CI. Happy to help fix all of these, the effort will be fairly minor (well, not sure about `pyregion`).

We did some minor tests. The tests in the repo run and we ran through some HST and JWST data and made sure at least that minimum functionality works. 

Happy to iterate on this. 

Cheers,
-Iva

  * For mobile there should be 1 result per row.

* There should be a button to allow the user to fetch a new set of 8 random dogs.

* The app should support common formats such as jpg, gif, png and mp4 results (if you encounter any totally random file types like psd just ignore that result and fetch another in its place)

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: tuckerbabcock
body:
This merges all the changes I've made to the magnetostatic solver to make it support evaluation on 2D meshes. Includes all the EM outputs needed for a motor problem, with all of them differentiated.

Items of potentially broad interest:

- `RelaxedNewtonSolver`: a newton solver that supports various `LineSearch` methods. Currently only have a backtracking linesearch implemented that fits a quadratic or cubic and calculates the step as the step that minimizes the fit polynomial.

- Further developed support for reverse and forward mode output and residual sensitivities

- Maybe more?

author: dougburke
body:
If dmimgcalc is given an opstr that's "too long" (for some ill-defined criterion of what too long actually is) we switch to using the stack support, which is new in CIAO 4.15. We could always do so, but

a) let's not break things we know already work
b) not using a stack here is a bit cleaner

We do not change how dmimgcalc_add works, since even though it could take advantage of this, we have code that seems to work, and there may be some advantage of adding data in chunks rather than all-in-one go, primarily in the amount of memory used at the expense of header/metadata shenanighans.

There are some minor code-style tweaks.

author: spalger
body:
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/145129

In order to make our TS setup in the repo far more efficient we needed to make it a little more complicated than it used to be. This includes a few rules that all tsconfig files need to follow which were currently assumed to be true, but with this PR will now be validated:

1. No tsconfig.json files are allowed to extend the `tsconfig.json` file. This file is used to produce types for the root of the repo, and include the `package.json` file in a project so it can be referenced in projects directly. Files which violate this rule were updated to point to the root `tsconfig.base.json` file.
2. Every tsconfig.json file must extend the `tsconfig.base.json` file, either directly or indirectly.

body:
## Motivation / Problem

In Scenario Editor, we can build canals by area, but in-game we are restricted to building a single-tile-wide canal in one action.

This restriction feels arbitrary and makes building things like this slower:

![canal](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/55058389/201742860-85900948-0e10-4d8d-86b1-6bca37706e78.png)

## Description

Remove the arbitrary restriction on building an area of canal tiles outside Scenario Editor.

I believe this follows a precedent set by #9709 and #10027 where we make it easier for players to build more objects or purchased tiles at once.

I can't think of an exploit that limiting canal construction could be trying to prevent, that wouldn't be an issue with other terraforming.

## Limitations

It is not possible to build canals diagonally with Ctrl like rivers in Scenario Editor, because the Ctrl key is already used to modify the canal tool to flood dry tiles into sea, when in Scenario Editor on dry sea-level tiles.

## Checklist for review

Some things are not automated, and forgotten often. This list is a reminder for the reviewers.
* The bug fix is important enough to be backported? (label: 'backport requested')
* This PR touches english.txt or translations? Check the [guidelines](https://github.com/OpenTTD/OpenTTD/blob/master/docs/eints.md)
* This PR affects the save game format? (label 'savegame upgrade')
* This PR affects the GS/AI API? (label 'needs review: Script API')

author: evan-ctl
body:
Noticed during a few things during a check for the `webpack` update:
* I had forgotten to pull the current state of `econplayground.js` into my local master branch, so I had to replace the ones that were edited during the `econplayground.js` clean-up.
* The build wasn't connecting to the build files made in the `/media/js/` but the old files in the`/econplayground.js/` directory of the `econplayground` repo.
* That "Loading..." feature that was implemented for displaying graphs which lack a `gType` property breaks the `Linear Demand and Supply` graph. It might be that it is the default and a `gType` is either not assigned or passed when that graph option is called. If we want to put something in place then we'll need to remove that graph as the default.
    * See this commit for what I believe caused the issue: https://github.com/ccnmtl/econplayground.js/commit/81d231821e47a4e18f3bbf384c9534b795f92bb7

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: jeffchuber
body:
- added a delete endpoint
- if `environment` is `test` - dont send errors to sentry
- added 2 `posthog` telemetry notices for index generation and results generation
- send through the `environment` by default through to `posthog`
- enable sending through single strings for logging arrays of new embeddings for `dataset` and `space_key`
- added 2 forms of pagination to fetch, by `limit`+`offset` or by `page`+`page_size`
- added the ability to call `chroma.count(all=True)` to override the default `space_key`
- more tests! 

Notes
- we keep `post` for more endpoints than I really would like. But for those endpoints we need to send the `json` `where_filter` through and this is annoying to do with `get`. 
- we set `mutations_sync` to 1 so that it forces `DELETE` to be run synchronously and our tests for delete to pass without an arbitrary sleep statement... I am not sure how this affects performance of INSERT. It doesn't seem to in limited testing, but worth keeping an eye on, and this is a breadcrumb for that.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

```

Target /usr/local/bin/2to3-3.11
already exists. You may want to remove it:
  rm '/usr/local/bin/2to3-3.11'
```

Installing llvm with --overwrite didn't seem to pass it on dependencies, particularly python (https://github.com/carbon-language/carbon-lang/actions/runs/3464174572/jobs/5785378508). So this instead installs python separately, and then --overwrite works.

author: albertz
body:
When any cell-based unit (e.g. `ZoneoutLSTM`) was used as a unit in the `RecLayer`, the variable names were different depending on whether the layer was operating on a per-step basis or on a sequence. Namely, in the latter case, it was using `rnn.dynamic_rnn`, which added the scope `"rnn"`. Thus, in one case, parameters looked like `layer/rec/lstm_cell/kernel`, and in the other case, they looked like `layer/rec/rnn/lstm_cell/kernel`.

Automatic param mapping when loading a model hid this bug because it still worked. However, with returnn-common, this bug became visible.

author: abudup
body:
### Description
Improve the profile explorer by enabling shape sensitivity for GPU kernels.



### Motivation and Context
Due to problems with the ROCM profiler, it was previously challenging to retrieve the shapes corresponding to a GPU kernel event. [PR 13546](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/pull/13549) addresses these problems, so it's now possible to retrieve shapes from the ORT ROCM/CUDA profilers. This PR leverages [PR 13546](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/pull/13549) to enable shape-sensitive GPU kernel ranking.

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: zihanchen-msft
body:
## Summary

The current implementation think `{[key:T]:U}` and `{key:object}` are the same type, which is semantically wrong.

This pull request fixes the problem and return `{type:'GenericObjectTypeAnnotation'}`, so that `{[key:T]:U}` is `Object`. The current schema cannot represent dictionary type, `Object` is the closest one.

The previous incorrect implementation actually bring in code with logic that doesn't make sense (treating indexer as property), those and related unit test are all undone.

## Changelog

[General] [Changed] - Fix codegen output for object with indexer

## Test Plan

`yarn jest react-native-codegen` passed

author: neelvirdy
body:
`TestNDuplicateNamesNDuplicateUsersNTimeWork` and `TestNDuplicateNamesNDuplicateUsersNTimeWork5Workers` tests were flaky, primarily due to `PinningOperation`'s `contid` being set to the `userid` for test data. In digging through this, found a couple other clean ups.

1. Manually assign `contId` in `newPinData` to have more control over test cases. This ensures N*N work is done when N users are uploading N different conts, for example. Previously `userid` was used for `contid`.
2. Lock for initial `popNextPinOp` in case `Run` gets called multiple times
3. Only have workers `doPinning` if `op` is not nil, which lets us avoid setting `send` to nil when `next` is nil

body:
basic implementation for a `AsyncLogger` that submits logging jobs that do not block the main process.

current implementation uses a threadpool, however should further evaluate tradeoffs with process pool, and potential future need for a more sophisticated job worker

open questions:
* how to best propagate errors after jobs have been submitted and user requests have been returned. currently issuing a python `error` log that displays the error message however this is more of a "silent" failure which is not ideal - a separate job worker may be able to better handle this
* exploration of limitations of executors and potential overhead added

**test_plan:**
included tests to verify that calls are non blocking, numpy arrays and functions may be submitted, verification of job run and error propagation

more thorough testing should be added in E2E tests

author: trellixvulnteam
body:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

author: renfraser
body:
When `'unsafe-eval'` is used on a web page, cypress-axe can't run because the `injectAxe()` function calls `window.eval()`. 

From [the Mozilla docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/eval):

> Warning: Executing JavaScript from a string is an enormous security risk. It is far too easy for a bad actor to run arbitrary code when you use eval(). See Never use eval()!, below. 

This commit updates the `injectAxe()` function to remove `eval` so that users of `unsafe-eval` can still use cypress-axe without having to override the `injectAxe()` function.
